title: Primitive recursion inside Peano arithmetic

based_on.title: Provability logic: models within models in Peano Arithmetic
An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: A finite recursive recipe gives one arithmetic proof of totality, uniqueness and its defining equations.
abstract: Having a proof for each numerical calculation does not give a single proof that every input has an answer. Peano arithmetic can prove that stronger assertion for every function built by primitive recursion. Starting from the function’s recursive construction, we build an arithmetic formula for its graph and prove that every input has exactly one output. Coded computation histories make the induction steps possible. The system also proves the defining equations, allowing further proofs about the function, such as an inductive proof that a doubling program returns the input added to itself. Agreement on ordinary numerical inputs alone would not justify those steps.
